messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher service surge. memory growth >95% on node gpu-usw2-47, kernel OOMs and SIGABRT observed, ~40% 5xx across us-west. link: https://infra/alerts/4312345678 

morgan: I'm oncall — seeing paging and node flaps for batcher. customers in dedicated us-west showing 5xx and 10x latency. paging indicators + swap churn. paging-related OOM? Paging spike started ~T-6m. Paging + CUDA errors together. Paging counts: prefetcher spiked. Paging link: https://metrics/graphs/cont-batcher/paging

kai: on it. which pool and which pod? can someone paste last pod logs and dmesg?

incident-bot: Event summary: service=continuous-batcher, pod=batcher-4f7b9, node=gpu-usw2-47, last_event=SIGABRT (pid 2413), oom_kill: yes, stack=continuous-batcher-v2, related alerts: cuda-error, kernel-oom, prefetch-rate-spike

riley: jumping in. grabbing pod logs + kv-cache_stats. early look: prefetch_rate jumped x40 for a short window; accumulator kept growing. suspect prefetch ramp -> uncontrolled batch accumulation -> big KV cache and then paging on GPU memory -> CUDA OOM -> kernel OOM -> sigabrt.

riley: logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-14T21:03:12Z] batcher: accept req id=0x9f3 acc=8123 batch_size=4096 bytes=3.2G
[2026-03-14T21:03:13Z] kvcache: prefetch queue length=12345 prefetch_rate=4100/s
[2026-03-14T21:03:13Z] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY in mkernel.cu:242
[2026-03-14T21:03:13Z] kernel: [OOM] kill process 2413 (batcher) score 900
[2026-03-14T21:03:14Z] signal: SIGABRT pid=2413
```

jen: recommended immediate mitigations: 
- disable prefetcher flag (FF_PREFETCH=off)
- set BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT=4 and BATCH_MAX_BYTES=64MB
- reduce in-memory KV prefetch window to 1s
- cordon + drain gpu-usw2-47
- enable model fallback to small-quant variant for us-west until root cause is fixed

morgan: applying flags now. @ops-bot cordon gpu-usw2-47 and drain batcher pods. I'll also enable the fallback.

ops-bot: kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-47 --reason="paging-OOM-surge" -> done
ops-bot: kubectl drain gpu-usw2-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -> evicted batcher pods, restarted on gpu-usw2-49 and gpu-usw2-50

riley: after drain and FF, memory usage fell back to normal on the remaining nodes. however one restarted node reported a CUDA kernel panic / illegal instruction during startup: dmesg shows 'NVIDIA: kernel panic - illegal instruction in module nv_peer_mem' — possible driver mismatch after last kernel/driver rollout.

kai: if driver rollback isn't trivial, fallback + throttling is the path of least customer impact. Jen, can you flip the model-variant flag? Also add short-term rate limiting for the highest-throughput endpoints.

jen: flipped FLAG_MODEL_FALLBACK=small-quant for region us-west; set per-route rate-limit to 50rps burst 200 for generation endpoints. Applying BATCH_MAX_BYTES=64MB and BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT=4 in the runtime config.

morgan: metrics (T+8m): 5xxs from the impacted customers down from 40% -> 3%, p99 latency back to baseline for most routes. customer impact summary for CS: 2 Dedicated tenants experienced degraded throughput for ~12m, 5 customers saw transient 5xx spikes, no data loss.

emma: CS note — notified the two affected customers; sending incident advisory and expected ETA for full recovery. They're asking if this will reoccur.

riley: temporary mitigation seems effective. I grabbed core dumps from one of the OOMed pods and dmesg from the flapping node. Early hypothesis: combination of prefetcher bug (no backpressure when cached requests spike) + recent driver/kernel subtle incompatibility -> kernel-level CUDA panic on restart -> node OOMs and sigabrt in process. Need to prevent prefetch runaway with guardrails (circuit breaker) and pin driver/kernel.

kai: handoff plan: I'll stay for 30m to make sure no regressions, then hand off to next oncall. Riley to own postmortem and patch (prefetch guard + config default limits + monitoring alerts for prefetch_rate), Jen to own feature-flag rollback plan and model routing adjustments, Morgan leads RCA doc.

morgan: immediate action items (short):
- riley: write postmortem + attach core dumps and dmesg (owner)
- jen: ship config default change and add FF to disable prefetch by default on high-throughput pools
- kai: coordinate driver/kernel pin with infra (follow-up ticket)
- ops: run a quick fleet scan for nodes with the same driver/kernel combo and cordon if unstable

kai: adding followup tickets: INFRA-3481 (driver pin), BATCH-7229 (prefetch guardrails), MON-5577 (prefetch_rate alert + runbook).

incident-bot: Incident 4312345678 acknowledged by morgan (severity S2). Timeline created, Pager duty notified for handoff.

morgan: handing off now to next oncall (kai -> next). leaving notes in the incident doc. If anything spikes, tag #oncall-escalation. Good job team :thumbsup:
